analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The changed ranges are line 519 (head) and lines 1145-1146, per file_changes. The supplied patch is truncated and shows only the line 519 change. That change adds `--runtime-concurrency <sizes>` and `--runtime-stagger` to the runtime-generation benchmark documentation, with `RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark` as a code reference. The 1145-1146 head ranges fall in the benchmark flag table. Base lines 1143-1146 already document `--runtime-generation`, the assistant directory, and the KV quantization flags. I could not see the exact head text of 1145-1146 and treat it as an unverified documentation edit.

I found no security-relevant change. This is documentation only, with no source, config, or auth path modified. The documented flags are local diagnostic benchmark options. They do not touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), the attestation chain (TB-009/TB-011), or the key custody assets (A-002, A-003, A-015, A-016). Prefix caching stays off in these runs, and the document says so at base line 1155. That keeps T-041 unaffected: no SSD cache is written, so the at-rest surface, TTL, HMAC names, and the SEC-035 TTFT oracle are unchanged.

Remaining questions for integration: the new `RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark` code is not in this batch. Whether concurrent or staggered runs keep prefix cache off, avoid logging prompt plaintext (A-001), and avoid exposing identifiers cannot be verified from the supplied text. If a source change ships alongside this doc change, it should be reviewed against TB-007 and T-028. No documentation claim in the visible text weakens a stated threat-model control.
